method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of every definition and proof, sign-by-sign replay of the encoded tableau and transitivity construction, exact comparison of formulas, macros, protected tokens and identifiers, and count comparison for lists and tagged problems; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Tableau-based proof-theoretic notions: theoremhood, derivability, consistency, reflexivity, monotonicity, transitivity via Cut, the inconsistency characterization and proof-theoretic compactness.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section contrasts semantic notions with proof-theoretic notions defined through closed tableaux. A theorem A has a closed tableau for false A. A is derivable from Gamma when some finite subset of Gamma, signed true together with false A, has a closed tableau. Gamma is inconsistent when some finite subset, signed true, has a closed tableau; otherwise it is consistent.
samples.checks: The semantic triad, soundness/completeness link, both Proves notations, finite-premise witnesses, signs and closed-tableau conditions are all preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Reflexivity follows because if A belongs to Gamma, the finite singleton {A} supports the two-node closed tableau containing false A and true A. Monotonicity follows because every finite subset of Gamma is also a finite subset of a superset Delta.
samples.checks: The membership and subset directions are unchanged. The sole encoded tableau preserves both signs, the two assumption labels, nesting and the close marker.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For transitivity, choose finite C-premises from Delta witnessing derivability of B from A and Delta, and finite D-premises from Gamma witnessing derivability of A. Start a tableau with false B and all true C- and D-premises, apply Cut to A, and attach the two closed witness tableaux to the true-A and false-A branches. This proves derivability from Gamma union Delta and yields the stated iterated consequences.
samples.checks: All signs, finite-set inclusions, Cut branches and conclusion formulas are exact after the documented OLTAB-005 projection. OLTAB-005 repairs the source's ill-typed D-premise subset expression by placing braces around the finite set.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A set is inconsistent exactly when it derives every sentence. The proof is left as an exercise, with separate protected cross-references for the first-order and propositional builds.
samples.checks: The universal quantification over sentences, both tagged problem variants, file identifiers and proposition reference are preserved exactly.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Proof-theoretic compactness states that derivability already has a finite witnessing subset and that consistency follows when every finite subset is consistent. The proof reuses the finite closed-tableau witness for the first part and argues contrapositively for the second: inconsistency supplies a finite inconsistent subset.
samples.checks: Both proposition items and both proof items retain their directions, finite witnesses, signed premise sets and consistency conclusions.

source_observations: OLTAB-005 documents and repairs the transitivity proof's expression D_1, ..., D_m subseteq Gamma as the finite-set inclusion {D_1, ..., D_m} subseteq Gamma.
The repair is forced by the derivability definition, the parallel Delta_0 witness and the subsequent use of every D_i as a true-signed assumption.
The unit contains 1 oltableau environment, 4 enumerated items and 2 tagged problem environments in both source and target.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi compounds for proof-theoretic notions and tableau terminology remain open to expert correction under the existing terminology ledger.
The Cut attachment argument is prose-level rather than an encoded full tableau and was checked by reconstructing its two witness branches.
